To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we derived simple expressions for the nuclear–Coulomb scattering length a and effective range r0 in terms of the P matrix of strong interaction, and applied them to some exactly solvable hard-core models of strong interaction.

the nuclear-Coulombo low-energy scattering parameters are expressed in terms of the P-matix and that, for the models of strong interaction with hard core repulsion considered, these parameters can be obtained explicitly.
the nuclear-Coulom low-energy scattering parameters are determined by the residual P matrix and can be found analytically for some simple models of strong interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems.
the description of the interaction of charged hadrons in the P-matrix formalism and the derivation of the low-energy nuclear-Coulomb parameters in terms of the P matrix.

a generalization of the method of isolat-ing the background P matrix to the case of two charged hadron scattering, with the derivation of simple explicit expressions for the low-energy scattering parameters in terms of the P matrix of purely Coulomb interaction and the residual P matrix of nuclear interaction, and with the explicit calculation of the low-energy nuclear-Coulomb parameters for several models of finite-range nuclear interaction containing a hard core.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the P-matrix method combined with the method for isolating the background term is a powerful and convenient tool for studying nuclear-Coulomb interaction at low energies.
the nuclear-Coulob low-energy scattering parameters can be expressed in a simple explicit form in terms of the P matrix of the residual strong interaction.
the P matrix is the best and simplest tool for studying the interaction of two charged hadronic particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the P-matrix description of the two-body interaction of two charged hadron systems is very useful for investigating low-energy nuclear-Coulomb phenomena.
the method of isolat- ing the background term from the total P matrix is applicable in the case of two charged hadron scattering.

the P-matrix description of two-charged-hadron interaction combined with the method for isolating the Coulomb background P-matrix allows one to obtain the nuclear-Couloub low-energy scattering parameters in the form of a general formula, which is applicable to arbitrary models of strong interaction with finite range.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in contrast to the case of the purely Coulomb interaction of two charged hadron, the nuclear-Cou-lomb low-energy scattering lengths and effective ranges are not equal for the same values of the orbital quantum number, and, moreover, they do not coincide with the corresponding parameters for the purely Coulombelectrostatic interaction.

, in the case of two charged hadron interaction, the nuclear-Columb low-energy scattering parameters are not determined uniquely, but are determined by the residual P-matrix element, which depends on the model of finite-range strong force.
the method of isolat- ing the background term in the P matrix is a useful tool for the investigation of nuclear-Coulomb interactions at low energies.
